topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic establishes the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and foundational concepts of cancer progression and hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and survival signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades drive autonomous proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Blocks in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how impaired cell differentiation arrests tissues in proliferative progenitor states in both hematological and epithelial cancers.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptotic cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how genetic alterations disrupting p53, Bax, and BCL2 signaling permit cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere biology, and senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms of telomere shortening, TERT reactivation, and p53-dependent senescence that govern cellular lifespan and growth control.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and utilize oncometabolites to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascular recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how developing tumors trigger new blood vessel growth to overcome hypoxia and obtain nutrient perfusion.

topics.label: Mechanisms and genomic features of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the stages of systemic tumor dissemination, the seed-and-soil dynamics of colonization, and the clonal genomic features of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on cancer hallmarks, literature recommendations, and practical arrangements.
